content: 1. In 2016, R. Anum and P. Peña-Rosas, along with M. Garcia-Casal, published a comprehensive analysis of global maize production, utilization, and consumption in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences. This study provided detailed insights into the role of maize in global food systems. 2. The Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) released a report in 1992 titled Maize in Human Nutrition, which is part of the FAO Food and Nutrition Series. This document explored the nutritional significance of maize and its impact on human health. 3. Peña-Rosas, Garcia-Casal, Pachón, McLean, and Arabi discussed technical considerations for fortifying maize flour and cornmeal in public health programs in a 2014 publication in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences. Their work summarized the rationale and outcomes of expert consultations on this topic. 4. J. Gwirtz and M. Garcia-Casal examined the processing of maize flour and cornmeal food products in a 2014 article in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences. Their research focused on the technological aspects of maize processing and its implications for food quality and nutrition. 5. The Grain Inspection, Packers, and Stockyards Administration established United States standards for corn, which were documented in a publicly accessible PDF as of August 31, 2016. These standards ensure the quality and safety of corn products in the U.S. market. 6. T. Stiver authored a technical bulletin in 1955 on American corn milling systems for producing de-germed products. This bulletin, published by the International Association of Operative Millers, provided a detailed overview of milling technologies and their applications. 7. J. Wingfield compiled a Dictionary of Milling Terms and Equipment in 1989, offering a comprehensive reference for professionals in the milling industry. This work was also published by the International Association of Operative Millers. 8. Bressani, Rooney, and Saldivar reviewed the fortification of corn masa flour with iron and other nutrients in a literature and industry experience report. This document, accessed in 2016, highlighted the benefits and challenges of fortification practices. 9. Ocheme, Oludamilola, and Gladys investigated the effects of lime soaking and cooking (nixtamalization) on the proximate, functional, and anti-nutritional properties of millet flour. Their findings were published in the Assumption University Journal of Technology. 10. Rivero, Racca, Martinez-Torres, Taylor, Trooper, and colleagues studied the fortification of precooked maize flour with coarse defatted maize germ. Their research, published in 1994 in the Archives of Latin American Nutrition, demonstrated the nutritional benefits of this fortification approach. 11. Dar and colleagues explored the multifactorial decision-making process involved in fortifying staple foods with iron in a 2002 article in Nutrition Reviews. Their discussion emphasized the importance of considering various factors to optimize public health outcomes. 12. Allen, de Benoist, Dary, and Hurrell edited the Guidelines on Food Fortification with Micronutrients, which was made available in 2016. This document serves as a key resource for implementing effective fortification programs. 13. The Food Fortification Initiative provided an online resource accessed on August 31, 2016, offering guidance and tools for fortifying staple foods to improve public health. 14. Hamner and Tinker reviewed the fortification of corn masa flour with folic acid in the United States in a 2014 publication in the Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences. Their work summarized the evidence supporting this intervention. 15. The World Health Organization (WHO) released guidelines on the fortification of maize flour and cornmeal with vitamins and minerals. These recommendations aim to address micronutrient deficiencies in vulnerable populations. 16. WHO, UNICEF, WFP, and UNHCR collaborated on a consultation regarding the dietary management of moderate malnutrition in children under five years old. Their findings were published in the Food and Nutrition Bulletin in 2009. 17. Nuss and Tanumihardjo highlighted the importance of maize as a staple crop in global nutrition in a 2010 article in Comprehensive Reviews in Food Science and Food Safety. Their analysis underscored maize's role in addressing food security and malnutrition. 18. Dar, Freire, and Kim developed guidelines for using iron compounds in food fortification programs in Latin America and the Caribbean. Their recommendations were published in Nutrition Reviews in 2002. 19. Garcia-Casal, Peña-Rosas, De-Regil, Gwirtz, and Pasricha conducted a Cochrane systematic review in 2016 on the fortification of maize flour with iron to prevent anemia and iron deficiency in populations. 20. Gera, Sachdev, and Boy systematically reviewed the effects of iron-fortified foods on hematologic and biological outcomes in randomized controlled trials. Their findings were published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2012.
